note: ادھر means here/this way/on this side and contextually over there/that way. 'Yonder' is archaic learner English and the entry can be clearer.
proposed_english: here; this way; on this side; over there/that way (context-dependent)

note: کلو is used as a nickname/name and can refer to a dark/black-colored person or thing; the latter can be derogatory when referring to skin. The same written form is also the common modern loanword 'kilo/kilogram', which the existing repair still omits.
proposed_english: Kallu/Kallo (nickname/name); dark/black-colored person or thing (can be derogatory when referring to skin); kilo/kilogram (loanword, context-dependent)

note: ٹھیک very commonly means okay/fine/correct/right as well as exactly/properly. The current gloss omits the basic conversational meanings.
proposed_english: okay; fine; correct; right; exactly; properly

note: نقشہ centrally means map and also plan/layout/diagram/blueprint. Omitting 'map' is a major learner defect.
کریم is a major homograph: karīm means generous/noble and is a common name; cream is also borrowed as کریم. The source lists only the given name.
ابو is commonly used for dad/father and is also Arabic Abū 'father of' in names/kunyas. Defining it only as a diminutive of ابا is not learner-friendly.
proposed_english: dad; father; Abu/father of (in Arabic-style names and kunyas)

note: دفعہ very commonly means time/occasion ('once/twice') and section/article/clause in legal texts. The source's 'group; class in school' misses these core senses.
proposed_english: time; occasion; section; article; clause (especially legal)

note: راستے is an inflected form of راستہ and must explicitly give road/way/route/path rather than only inflection labels.
proposed_english: roads; ways; routes; paths; road/way (oblique/vocative singular, context-dependent)

note: وسیع means wide/broad/extensive/spacious and is an adjective, not a noun.
غیرت means honor/self-respect/sense of dignity and can involve modesty/shame in cultural contexts. 'Shame; bashfulness' alone risks reversing the core meaning.
proposed_english: honor; self-respect; dignity; sense of honor; modesty/shame (context-dependent)

note: مرکز centrally means center/centre/hub/headquarters. 'Capital' can occur contextually but 'centerpoint' is awkward learner English.
proposed_english: center; centre; hub; headquarters; central point

note: انکار centrally means refusal/denial/rejection. 'Deviation; abstinence; refrain' are not appropriate core learner glosses.
کھانا means food/meal and to eat. 'Cooked rice' is not the ordinary general meaning and should be removed.
موضوع centrally means topic/subject/theme. The source instead lists etymological participial senses such as placed/manufactured and omits the basic learner meaning.
پیدائش means birth/origin/creation. 'Wages, earnings' is erroneous source contamination.
دار is widely used as a suffix meaning holder/possessor/having (e.g. ذمہ دار) and as a noun for gallows in another reading. 'Seat; wife; wood' is unrelated source noise.
جنہیں is a plural oblique/dative relative pronoun meaning whom/which/to whom or which. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
proposed_english: whom; which; to whom; to which (plural)

note: کرو is the extremely common familiar/plural imperative of کرنا meaning 'do!/make!'. The source instead leads with the mythological proper name Kuru and omits the Urdu verb meaning.
proposed_english: do!; make! (imperative form of کرنا); Kuru (proper name, rare/context-dependent)
